text: Owner decision 2026-07-21: the logical-map Artifact mirror (claude.ai/code/artifact/f20dda86-f0ac-4dba-b2a1-a191e6c3b034) is RETIRED — never republish it after map changes. Fully redundant with the permanent public Pages URL, and each republish costs an unavoidable web permission prompt (claude.ai web sessions apply no permission allowlists). The map's only maintained home is docs/site/logical-map.html served via Pages.

Owner decision 2026-07-21: docs/site/repo-map.html (physical-folders view) is deleted; docs/site/logical-map.html is the repo's single map. The add-a-file inventory drill now touches ONE map (SELF frame counts + Σ), CLAUDE.md layout table, and this file. Legacy stub docs/repo-map.html redirects to the logical map.

GitHub REST and GraphQL enforce SEPARATE rate-limit pools, and the GitHub MCP mixes them within one PR flow: merge_pull_request is REST, while update_pull_request(draft:false) is GraphQL-only (markPullRequestReadyForReview — GitHub exposes no REST equivalent). Proven 2026-08-01 on PR #187: the merge call returned a clean 405 'still a draft' while the un-draft call returned 'rate limit already exceeded for user ID 108373010'. Consequences: (1) a GraphQL strike does NOT block merging an already-non-draft PR; (2) un-draft as soon as CI is green rather than at merge time; (3) when a session is GraphQL-blocked on a green PR, the owner clicking 'Ready for review' alone unblocks it — no need to wait out the rolling hour.

A UI suite written from the implementation confirms the implementation. Proven 2026-08-01 on claude.directives' repo map: a 27-assertion Playwright gate stayed green through four consecutive interaction bugs the owner found by looking at the page — header overlay, 10px drag handle, wheel-zooms-instead-of-panning, and arrows routed through boxes. Each assertion drove the app the way the author built it (page.click by selector; mouse.down+move, never a wheel or touch event) and checked a mechanism rather than a visible outcome. The crossing check also only ever ran on the shipped layout, so it proved nothing about a layout the reader rearranged. Rule now exported as directives/test.md -> 'Assert the outcome, not the mechanism': name the observable outcome first, exercise the whole input surface (pointer/wheel/touch/keyboard), perturb the state before re-asserting, and when a human reports a defect the suite passed, ship the missing assertion alongside the fix.

Considered and REJECTED changing the PR-draft default to open PRs ready-for-review. Raised 2026-08-04 after an exhausted GraphQL quota blocked un-drafting on three consecutive green PRs (#199, #200, #201), each stalling until the owner clicked 'Ready for review'. git.md lines 125-131 already reasoned through this exact trade in July and prescribes the mitigation: keep draft-on-first-push (global.md -> PR Lifecycle) but leave draft AS SOON AS CI IS GREEN, not at merge time, so the GraphQL call happens while budget remains. That rule was being followed; what exhausted the pool was session volume (7 PRs plus heavy API reads in one session), not the draft policy. Reversing a deliberate prior ruling would not have addressed the cause. Per-PR judgement to open ready-for-review remains available when a session is already quota-strained (used on #202/#203, merged without stalling) — that is a judgement call, not a policy change.

Creating a PR subscribes the session to its activity HARNESS-SIDE — no tool call is involved and none is needed. subscribe_pr_activity exists to take over a PR the session did not open, or to re-subscribe after unsubscribing; calling it after your own create_pull_request is a no-op that reads as the thing that caused the subscription. Discovered 2026-08-14 while scoping PR #214 (closed) and never written to a file until now: directives/git.md's PR Lifecycle line had said 'Subscribe to PR activity via subscribe_pr_activity immediately after opening', which misdescribed the mechanism without being harmful. Matters because a session reasoning from that line will believe it can prevent subscription by omitting the call, which is false — the only lever is unsubscribe_pr_activity after the fact.

The codex-flagged label is applied ASYNCHRONOUSLY by codex-monitor.yml, so absence of the label is not evidence that Codex has not flagged the PR. Observed 2026-08-14 on claude.directives#215: the Codex review landed 06:46:40, the merge went through at 06:47 with labels checked and clean, and three valid P1/P2 findings merged past the gate — all three were real and needed a follow-up PR. git.md's merge gate had said to check labels; checking labels alone loses every race where a review lands within the monitor's dispatch window. The gate now also requires reading the PR's reviews directly (pull_request_read -> get_reviews) on the current head immediately before merging. Generalises: any gate that reads a state a workflow WRITES is racing that workflow, and the fix is to read the underlying source rather than the derived marker.

Design note for the deferred ui-suite skipped-result gate (deliberately NOT built in #216 — it would change CI failure semantics for every downstream project). The naive gate is wrong twice over. First, failing on any skip would fail every project without auth configured: templates/ui-tests/tests/app.spec.js:230,322,456 skip the auth scenarios when TEST_AUTH_CREDENTIAL is empty, which the kit INTENDS. Second, the obvious refinement — fail only on skips lacking a reason string, since test.skip(condition, reason) carries one — does not separate deliberate from accidental either: a careful author writing a fixture-absence skip attaches a reason too ('no X with rows'), and that is exactly the coverage hole Codex flagged on #216 as the defect class to catch. Presence of a reason is therefore not the discriminator. What likely works is an explicit allowlist of approved skip identities (test id or exact reason string) checked against a JSON reporter run, so an intended skip is enumerated once and any NEW skip fails — the same shape as the secret-scan pattern check: enumerate the permitted set, fail on anything outside it. Unresolved and worth deciding before building: whether the allowlist lives in the repo under test or in the ui-suite action's defaults.
